_meta: Attention logits from one query to the first token and to a sliding window of recent tokens, used to show the ATTENTION SINK phenomenon and why a sliding-window KV cache must keep the first tokens. Trained transformers learn to dump excess attention -- attention they have no better place for -- onto the first token(s), which act as an attention SINK: the softmax must sum to 1, so when the query has little it genuinely wants to attend to, the leftover probability piles onto the sink instead of being forced onto content tokens. sink_logit is the query's (large, learned) attention score to the first token; window_logits are its scores to the recent tokens in the sliding window (their real relevances). With the sink present, softmax over [sink] + window gives the sink ~0.93 of the attention and leaves the window tokens with their small, correct weights (0.017, 0.006, 0.046) -- most attention parks on the sink. A naive sliding-window cache EVICTS the first tokens to save memory, so the softmax is taken over the window only: the sink's ~0.93 has nowhere to go and is forced onto the window tokens, ballooning their weights (0.245, 0.090, 0.665) and massively over-concentrating attention on recent tokens -- the quality collapse StreamingLLM identified. The fix is to keep a few initial sink tokens in the cache alongside the recent window. Note the relative order among window tokens is preserved (the strongest stays strongest), so the information is present; it is the magnitudes that are corrupted. sink_logit and window_logits are the fixture; every softmax weight, with and without the sink, is computed.
